edits.original: Breeders select dwarfing alleles on purpose, rather than by accident.
edits.replacement: Breeders select dwarfing alleles on purpose.
edits.reason: By accident is the ordinary-knowledge antonym of on purpose, so the trailer adds nothing and should be cut.

edits.original: The construct was designed for chloroplast transformation, not nuclear transformation.
edits.replacement: The construct was designed for chloroplast transformation. Its transgene integrates into the plastid genome.
edits.reason: Chloroplast-versus-nuclear insertion is a genuine, checkable distinction smuggled into a bolted-on 'not' clause, so it earns its own sentence stated as what the construct is.

edits.original: Conservation collections still accession landraces, rather than heirlooms.
edits.replacement: Conservation collections still accession landraces, rather than heirlooms.
edits.reason: Flagging rather than editing: 'heirloom' is not an ordinary-knowledge antonym of 'landrace', but the two categories overlap (heirlooms often are old landraces), so I am not sure whether this trailer is a genuine distinction deserving its own sentence or an inaccurate contrast; please confirm which side of the test it falls on.
